editorial:
Imagine working your heart out for a dream only to have it ripped away by someone else's mistake. That is exactly what happens to Kyung-hak. He is a hardworking guy trying to become a cop, but his life flips upside down when he inherits a massive debt from his mother. Instead of hitting the books, you will see him spending his days as a delivery driver just to survive. The vibe is heavy and realistic, showing you how money stress can slowly poison a happy relationship with a girlfriend who truly cares about you. It feels like a slice of real life that hits way too close to home for a lot of us.

You will really appreciate the acting here because it does not feel fake or over the top. The slow pace helps you feel the weight of his exhaustion, though some might find it a bit too quiet at times. If you enjoy stories about the struggle to survive and the pain of growing up, you should definitely give this a go.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a bittersweet note. After fighting through the stress of debt and a failing relationship, Kyung-hak realizes that his dreams have changed. He does not magically get rich or suddenly become a cop. Instead, he finds a way to accept his new reality and the distance between him and Hye-jin. It wraps up by showing that while life is unfair, moving forward is the only way to find peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves grounded stories about life struggles and romance.
